question: Which proof systems and circuit languages can I use for a zero-knowledge application on Stellar, how are proofs verified on-chain, and when is a trusted setup needed?

golden.answer: Stellar mandates no single toolchain: use Circom/Groth16, Noir (UltraHonk) or zkVMs such as RISC Zero, with a compatible Soroban verifier contract. The app team defines the circuit and keys. The verifier contract uses the native BLS12-381, BN254 and Poseidon host functions, which are primitives, not a private-payment system. A Groth16 proof verifies on BLS12-381 or BN254 only when the circuit and the verifier use the same curve. Circuit-specific Groth16 normally needs a trusted setup; transparent systems do not.
keyFacts: Stellar mandates no ZK toolchain; Circom/Groth16, Noir and RISC Zero verifiers exist.
A Soroban verifier contract checks proofs with native BN254 or BLS12-381 host functions.
Host functions are primitives; they do not make payments private automatically.
Circuit-specific Groth16 normally needs a trusted setup; transparent systems do not.
avoid: Do NOT claim Noir is the only supported route, or that Protocol 25 makes every payment private.
golden.notes: As of 2026-11-14 the OpenZeppelin confidential-token UltraHonk verifier accepts only non-zero-knowledge proofs; an answer that states this limit is correct.

corroboration.claim: Stellar does not require Noir; multiple proof systems and circuit languages can target Soroban verifiers.
Proofs are checked by compatible Soroban verifier logic, using native host functions where the curve and primitives match.
Protocol 25 provides BN254 and Poseidon/Poseidon2 building blocks, not an automatic private-payment system.
Noir is the only supported way to build ZK applications on Stellar.
Protocol 25 automatically makes every Stellar payment private.
As of 2026-11-02, the rs-soroban-ultrahonk Soroban verifier accepts only non-zero-knowledge UltraHonk proofs and gives no witness-hiding guarantee.
